_说明: 《千年一榫》界面英文词条表（中文原文即键；en 模式查本表，未命中回退中文+告警）。
结构：{"_说明":[…],"翻译":{"中文":"English"}}；"_" 前缀键加载器跳过。
术语表：榫卯=mortise-tenon (sunmao)；锐眼=Keen Eye；天赋值=Talent；衣橱=Wardrobe；
见证者=the Witness；晷=Gui；体素=voxel；河姆渡=Hemudu；宋/元/明=Song/Yuan/Ming；
现代=Modern；未完待续=To be continued；完美/良好/及格=Perfect/Good/Pass。
带参文案以 %s/%d 占位（键=整句模板，调用点 % 格式化）。
content_en.json（另一实施者产出，只读）加载序在本表之后、同键覆盖本表。

翻译.【河姆渡榫卯木构件】\n时间：距今约七千年的新石器时代（河姆渡文化）。\n地点：:
[Hemudu Mortise-Tenon Timber Members]
Era: Neolithic Age, about 7,000 years ago (Hemudu culture).
Place: Hemudu site, Yuyao, Zhejiang.
Type: Wooden mortise-tenon building members.
Significance: Among the earliest mortise-tenon artifacts ever discovered, regarded as the origin of Chinese timber construction.
翻译.【保国寺瓜棱柱斗拱】\n时间：北宋（11 世纪初）。\n地点：浙江宁波保国寺。\:
[Baoguo Temple Melon-Ribbed Columns and Bracket Sets]
Era: Northern Song (early 11th century).
Place: Baoguo Temple, Ningbo, Zhejiang.
Type: Wooden dougong brackets and melon-ribbed columns.
Significance: One of the oldest surviving timber buildings in Jiangnan, showing the maturity of Song-era mortise-tenon craftsmanship.
翻译.【真如寺梁架榫卯】\n时间：元代（14 世纪）。\n地点：上海真如寺。\n类型：:
[Zhenru Temple Timber Roof Frame]
Era: Yuan dynasty (14th century).
Place: Zhenru Temple, Shanghai.
Type: Wooden roof-frame mortise-tenon joinery.
Significance: A precious surviving Yuan-era roof frame, witnessing the continuity of mortise-tenon craft in vernacular architecture.
翻译.【明式黄花梨圈椅】\n时间：明代（15~17 世纪）。\n地点：江南地区。\n类:
[Ming-Style Huanghuali Round-Backed Chair]
Era: Ming dynasty (15th-17th century).
Place: Jiangnan region.
Type: Huanghuali wood furniture (round-backed chair).
Significance: A masterpiece of Ming furniture and the peak of mortise-tenon craft in everyday objects.
翻译.【参数化木构节点】\n时间：当代。\n地点：数字设计与工程实践。\n类型：参数化:
[Parametric Timber Joints]
Era: Contemporary.
Place: Digital design and engineering practice.
Type: Parametrically designed timber joints.
Significance: Marrying the mortise-tenon tradition with digital fabrication to explore the contemporary form of timber architecture.

翻译.本相者，万般神通之所自出——初心是也。粗布围裙裹未凿之璞，一手执刨，一手抱梁。围: True Form is the source of all arts — the original heart itself. A coarse apron wraps the uncarved raw wood; one hand holds the plane, the other embraces the beam. The deepest worn spot on that apron is where the plane has landed a thousand times.
翻译.玉尺者，宋人之神理也。素袍玉簪，袖中自有一部《营造法式》。以材为祖，以分为度，举: Jade Ruler is the spirit of Song principles. Plain robe, jade hairpin, and in the sleeve a whole Yingzao Fashi. Timber as the ancestor, fen as the measure; raises and slopes have numbers, bracket sets have scores — never off by a hair. Worn, your snapped lines follow the classics.
翻译.苍梁者，大木之雄也。毡帽革带，弯刀在腰，敢以巨额承千钧。佩之，胸怀便阔：梁不怕粗: Mighty Beam is the hero of heavy timber. Felt hat, leather belt, a curved knife at the waist — daring to bear a thousand jun with great measure. Worn, the heart broadens: beams fear not thickness, columns fear not girth; great timber has great uses — no need to trim the foot to fit the shoe.
翻译.缠枝者，线脚之神也。水墨衣带，当风婉转。巧不在力吼，而在圆熟：边抹起线一气贯通，: Intertwining Vine is the spirit of moldings. Ink-wash sash fluttering in the wind. The skill lies not in brute force but in roundness: edge lines flow in one breath, wrapped-leg curves show no sharp corners. Worn, even hardwood grows gentle.
翻译.衍数者，今之神机也。素衣执扇，扇中参数列列，榫卯纳于其中。古人运斤，今人运算；算: Parametrics is the modern marvel. Plain robes, a fan in hand; parameters arrayed across it, mortise and tenon held within. The ancients swung axes, we compute — yet at the finest of calculations, you still test the fit with your own hand. The breeze beneath that fan comes from millennia.
翻译.抱节者，雪豹山灵也。怀中竹筒，抱之如抱柱，寒天不放手。竹有节，木有理，榫有卯——: Bamboo Integrity is a snow-leopard mountain spirit. Clutching a bamboo tube to the chest like a pillar, never letting go in the cold. Bamboo has nodes, wood has grain, tenons have sockets — the node is the bone of wood and the faith of the carpenter. Worn, even the trickiest work keeps its measure.
翻译.运斤者，豹童也。红帔小槌，击竹有声，如磬如梆。匠石运斤成风，非力大，是心手相忘。: Axe Mastery is a leopard child. Red cape, small mallet, striking bamboo in chime-like beats. The master swung his axe like wind — not from strength, but a mind and hand grown one. Worn, the hammer lands true: where it falls is the ink line, stopping at seven-tenths of force.
翻译.髹饰者，狸奴也。对镜理奁，奁中是漆，镜里是器。披麻捉灰凡三层，方上漆，一器髹毕千: Lacquer Art is a cat companion. At the mirror tending a case; in the case, lacquer; in the mirror, the vessel. Hemp and paste laid thrice before the lacquer goes on — once finished, a piece endures a thousand years. Worn, every surface beneath your hand takes on a sheen.
翻译.煨木者，狐女也。掌中一釜，火候在心。欲曲一木，以文火徐煨，趁热就势，曲而不折。佩: Wood Bending is a fox maiden. A pot in her palm, the fire's temper in her heart. To bend a piece of wood, simmer it slowly over gentle heat and shape it while warm — bent, yet unbroken. Worn, haste learns to slow, and hardness learns to yield.
翻译.津梁者，九尾灵狐也。秉灯立于小桥，桥下花影，桥上灯明。桥是木作的菩萨心：肯弯腰，: Bridge of Mercy is a nine-tailed spirit fox. Lantern in hand upon a small bridge; flower shadows below, lamplight above. A bridge is the compassionate heart of woodworking: willing to bend, willing to bear. Worn, even at the direst pass a single thread of way opens.
翻译.斫轮者，莲上童子也。怀中一轮，徐徐而运。轮扁斫轮，得于手应于心，口不能言——真正: Wheel Wrighting is a child upon a lotus. A wheel in his arms, turned slowly round. Wheelwright Bian carved wheels with hand answering heart, beyond what words could tell — the true measure is not in books but in hands. Worn, the slower you go, the truer you land.
翻译.牵丝者，荷荡少年也。肩荷白藕，藕丝细如墨线，韧胜胶漆。藕断丝连，丝连者榫之神也：: Silk Thread is a youth of the lotus marshs. White lotus roots on his shoulder; their fibers fine as ink lines, tougher than glue and lacquer. The root breaks but fibers hold — that holding is the soul of the tenon: the piece may come apart, its spirit never does. Worn, all your hands touch carries on its old bond.
翻译.烹鲜者，炎童也。一手执串，一手掣火，火在肘腋而不燎眉。治木如烹鲜：文火焙之，猛火: Gentle Cooking is a child of flame. Skewer in one hand, fire in the other; flames at his elbow yet never singeing a brow. Treating wood is like cooking small fish: gentle heat to warm it, fierce fire to attack it — all depending on which the moment calls for. Worn, you know when to advance and retreat with dry timber.
翻译.执柯者，竹林豹女也。身负行囊，穿篁而过，叶声如雨。伐柯伐柯，其则不远——手中旧器: Timber Matching is a leopard maiden of the bamboo grove. Pack on her back, threading through the bamboo, leaves sounding like rain. Hew a handle, look to a handle — the model is never far: the old piece in your hand is what you learned from the last one. Worn, every stroke carries a lineage.
翻译.夯歌者，瓜田少年也。巨槌在肩，白犬相随，号子一起，落硪处尘土微颤。筑基不打诳语，: Ramming Song is a youth of the melon fields. A great mallet on his shoulder, a white dog at his heel; when the work chant rises, dust trembles where the rammer lands. Founding work tells no lies — every ram must land solid. Worn, the work beneath your feet is the most honest of all.
翻译.执矩者，顶瓜小童也。方瓜如玺，覆于头上——瓜可方，木亦可方。矩在头顶如在三尺上，: Square Rule is a small child with a gourd on his head. The square gourd sits like a seal — if a gourd can be squared, so can wood. With the square above the head as if three feet above, a straight heart draws a straight line. Worn, your cuts waste least and run true.
翻译.燔芝者，树栖游子也。青焰一簇，慢煨灵芝，白犬守于侧。火候急不得也熄不得，性子焙顺: Lingzhi Roasting is a wanderer of the treetops. A tuft of blue flame slowly roasting lingzhi, a white dog standing guard. The fire must neither be hurried nor quenched; once the temper is roasted smooth, the wood neither warps nor cracks. Worn, you can keep watch through the longest night.
翻译.磨镜者，卷发夫人也。手摇一磨，碾的是豆，磨的是性子。器面欲光，先磨其心。佩之，凡: Mirror Grinding is a lady of curled hair. Turning a hand mill — grinding beans, and grinding temper. Before a surface can shine, the heart must first be ground smooth. Worn, everything you finish polishes to a mirror, without a single burr.
翻译.悬河者，执壶夫人也。银膏一倾，如瀑倒悬，分寸全在腕底：多一线则溢，少一线则虚。佩: Pouring Stream is a lady with a ewer. Silver paste tips out like a waterfall hung upside down; the whole measure lies beneath the wrist — a hair too much and it overflows, a hair too little and it falls short. Worn, you can fill the cup full and still hold back the final drop.
翻译.白驹者，踏球小马也。蹄下有球，口衔一灯，灯不灭工不停。白驹过隙，千年一瞬，惟榫卯: White Colt is a small pony treading a ball. Beneath its hooves a sphere, in its mouth a lantern; while the lamp burns, the work goes on. A white colt flashes past a crack — a thousand years in an instant; only mortise and tenon can hold time in place. Worn, you grow familiar with time itself, and the work completes itself.
翻译.品泉者，执盏夫人也。啜饮之间，眉目安然。识材如品泉：一眼辨其性，一叩知其声。佩之: Spring Tasting is a lady with a cup. Between sips, her brows rest easy. Knowing timber is like tasting spring water: one glance tells its nature, one tap tells its voice. Worn, no piece of wood is misused — every material finds its proper place.
翻译.踩岁者，骑禽小娘子也。足下灵禽，一路碎响，如踏芝麻秸——碎碎平安，岁岁有今朝。佩: Stepping the Year is a young lady riding a wondrous bird. Under her feet crisp crackles all the way, like treading sesame stalks — crackle upon crackle, peace year upon year. Worn, every job starts with good omens, and every step lands on solid ground.
翻译.梅妆者，新岁贵人也。冠上梅开，鬓边龙影，喜气如披红。器物亦有妆：雕刻一两分，是给: Plum Adornment is a noble of the new year. Plum blossoms on the crown, a dragon's shadow at the temple — festive as wearing scarlet. Vessels too wear makeup: a stroke or two of carving dresses them in festive color. Worn, even the plainest timber blossoms.
翻译.伏枥者，火鬃小马也。卧于书箱之侧，鬃尾犹带余焰。老骥伏枥，歇着不是不走了。新材静: Stabled Steed is a small horse with flame-touched mane. Resting beside the book chest, mane and tail still carrying embers. The old steed lies in the stable — resting is not quitting. Fresh timber must season for years before it becomes a great vessel. Worn, you know when to strive and when to wait.
翻译.挑灯者，双灯童子也。赤发如焰，两肩挑灯。灯下看墨线，比日头下更直——心静了，线就: Lantern Bearer is a child with two lanterns. Fiery red hair, lanterns balanced on both shoulders. Under lamplight the ink line reads straighter than in daylight — when the heart is still, the line is straight. Worn, the long night has company, and the lamp lights itself.
翻译.鱼龙者，跨鲤童子也。鱼灯为骑，纸扇为鞭，一夜鱼龙舞。鱼灯骨架不过十几根竹篾，游起: Fish Dragon is a child astride a carp. A fish lantern for a mount, a paper fan for a whip — all night the fish and dragon dance. The lantern's frame is no more than a dozen bamboo strips, yet it swims like a living thing. Worn, everywhere you lift the heavy as if light, that is the craft.
翻译.向阳者，一株花也。陶盆浅土，终日随日头转身。木性亦然：受光面紧，背光面松——识得: Sunward is a single flower. A clay pot of shallow soil, turning with the sun all day long. Wood's nature is the same: tight on the lit side, loose on the shaded — know the sunny side and you know wood's temper. Worn, every cut follows the grain.
翻译.莳花者，蓝铃园丁也。草帽素裙，盆盆罐罐皆是活计。养木如养花：锄轻水匀，移对时辰。: Flower Planting is a bluebell gardener. Straw hat, plain skirt; pots and jars all her daily work. Curing wood is like growing flowers: hoe gently, water evenly, transplant at the right hour. Worn, everything passing through your hands slowly comes alive.
翻译.星涡者，衔烟斗的画师也。满身漩涡如星河倒卷——连天上的云都长成木纹。瘿木之涡，皆: Star Vortex is a painter with a pipe. Swirls over the body like a galaxy turned inside out — even the clouds in the sky grow into wood grain. The burls of gnarled wood are all drafts sketched by the years. Worn, you can read whole chapters in the roughest blank.
翻译.守拙者，画架上一卵也。不着一色，素到极处。大巧若拙——最高的手艺往往像没动手。佩: Humble Craft is an egg upon an easel. Not a stroke of color, plain to the utmost. Great skill seems clumsy — the highest craft often looks as if no hand had touched it. Worn, you will do the plodding work: only that one piece can be handed down ten years.
翻译.鉴形者，携镜少女也。卵者圆之极，镜者明之极。木匠以目为镜：梁直不直，吊起一望便知: Shape Mirror is a maiden carrying a mirror. The egg is the height of roundness, the mirror the height of brightness. The carpenter's eye is his mirror: hang the beam up, one look tells if it is true. Worn, heart clear and eyes bright — not a hair's crookedness gets past you.
翻译.守藏者，绿窗贵妇也。深坐雕木之阁，掌上明珠覆以琉璃。器物传到今天，靠的不是结实，: Keeper is a noble lady at the green window. Seated deep in a carved wooden chamber, the pearl in her palm covered with glass. What carries vessels down to today is not their sturdiness, but someone keeping them. Worn, every piece of old timber finds its place of honor.
翻译.结庐者，檐下小兽也。草亭一座，糖串一枚，躲在自家屋顶下。捆扎结顶是人类最早的房子: Hut Building is a small beast under the eaves. A thatched pavilion, a stick of candied haw, sheltering beneath its own roof. Tying poles into a roof was humanity's first house — before mortise and tenon, there was binding. Worn, you are a natural at starting from nothing.
翻译.绳墨者，帽肆匠人也。软尺一抖，尺寸了然。绳墨是匠人的规矩：曲直自此定，方圆自此分: Ink Line is a hatter-craftsman. One flick of the soft rule and every measure is known. The ink line is the carpenter's law: crooked or straight is settled here, square or round divided here — off by half a fen, you start over. Worn, you measure people and things alike, truly.
翻译.借景者，伞下夫人也。足下木台，一池睡莲，天光云影不请自来。造园贵在借：借远山，借: Borrowed Scenery is a lady beneath an umbrella. A wooden platform underfoot, a pool of water lilies; sky light and cloud shadows arrive uninvited. In garden-making all value lies in borrowing: borrow the distant hills, borrow the slanting sun. Worn, even the tiniest workshop holds heaven and earth.
翻译.叠石者，鸣镲小郎也。铜镲一击，石子三叠如小山。叠山讲一个「压」字：石互压而生稳，: Rock Stacking is a small lad with ringing cymbals. One strike, and pebbles stack threefold like a tiny hill. Stacking hills speaks one word: press — stones pressing one another grow stable, timbers pressing one another grow secure. Worn, even the most tangled situation can be set right.
翻译.穿山者，抱鳞小郎也。怀里金甲穿山兽，穿石如泥。凿卯如穿山：一寸一寸进，不响不噪，: Mountain Piercer is a small lad cradling a golden-scaled pangolin. Through stone as through mud. Chiseling a socket is like piercing a mountain: advance inch by inch, no clatter, no fuss, stop the moment you arrive. Worn, you dare to set chisel to the hardest wood.
翻译.凿岩者，冠兽小匠也。帽上金兽镇着，石槌起落，顽石让路。基在岩上，屋才立得千年——: Rock Chisel is a small craftsman crowned with a beast. The golden beast on his cap keeps guard; the stone mallet rises and falls, and stubborn rock gives way. A house stands a thousand years only when its base is on rock — the grandest roof frames all grow out of cracks in stone. Worn, you will do the groundwork.
翻译.启函者，破罐雏鸟也。一声脆响，天光灌进罐里——壳外还有天。开榫如启函：封得住才开: Opening the Case is a hatchling breaking its jar. One crisp crack and daylight floods in — beyond the shell there is more sky. Cutting a tenon is like opening a case: only what seals well can be opened well; what is not broken open stays dark. Worn, you dare the first chisel stroke at any deadlock.
翻译.理匣者，拾贝海娘也。珊瑚贝壳各归各位，一箱虽小，装得下一片海。收工如收箱：工具归: Box Tidying is a shell-gathering daughter of the sea. Coral and shells each in their place; a box small as it is, holds a whole sea. Ending work is like closing the box: tools return to their spots, offcuts into their slots. Worn, hand you a snarl of hemp and in a few strokes you will find the thread.
翻译.圆光者，水阁鲛后也。端坐圆窗之内，水母替她挑着水晶帘。圆光罩是木作绝活：一木镂空: Round Halo is the shark-queen of the water pavilion. Seated within the round window, jellyfish lifting her crystal curtain for her. The round-halo lattice is a woodworking marvel: one piece of wood carved hollow, divided yet unbroken. Worn, nothing divided or hidden gets past you.
翻译.悬鱼者，袋中金鳞也。碧水一囊，游鱼自在。古人在山墙悬一枚木鱼：水克火，木构最怕火: Hanging Fish is a golden-scaled fish in a bag. A pouch of clear water, fish swimming at ease. The ancients hung a wooden fish on the gable: water subdues fire, and timber frames fear fire most. Worn, you go out and in in safety — wherever you arrive, open flames restrain themselves.
翻译.落墨者，踏浪鲛姬也。符卷随身，朱印在侧，衣袂不湿。墨线一弹，百柱归位——纸上画符: Ink Snapping is a shark maiden treading the waves. Talismans about her, a vermilion seal at hand, her sleeves never wet. One snap of the ink line and a hundred columns find their places — talismans drawn on paper, lines snapped on wood. Worn, the first stroke lands true and no work needs redoing.
翻译.潜渊者，着褂渊童也。立于水底卵石之上，口吐珍珠，呼吸自如。沉得下去才浮得上来：木: Deep Diver is a child of the depths in a long jacket. Standing on pebbles at the water's bottom, breathing freely, pearls at his lips. Only one who can sink can rise: how much water a timber holds, one touch will tell. Worn, the deeper you go, the steadier you become.
翻译.负笈者，海府书生也。头顶墨玉，怀抱典籍，走一路读一路。书上得来的终究要过手——读: Book Carrier is a scholar of the sea court. Ink-jade on his head, classics in his arms, reading as he walks. What books give must finally pass through the hands — read ten thousand volumes, and hew ten thousand trees. Worn, any drawing you have seen once you know by heart.
翻译.横经者，贝阙观书人也。倚珠贝之床，周身明珠低照。手艺有止境，问学无止境。佩之，肯: Classic Reader is a reader at the shell gate. Leaning on a bed of pearls and shells, soft pearl light all around. Craft has its limits; learning has none. Worn, you will revisit old accounts: the errors and the clever turns of those before you, all remembered.
翻译.枕涛者，鲸月少年也。卧于贝床，耳边是一整片海。潮起潮落如千年松涛——木原是海的近: Wave Pillow is a youth of whale and moon. Lying on a bed of shells, a whole ocean sounding in his ears. Tides rising and falling like a thousand years of pine soughing — wood is, after all, the sea's close kin. Worn, where the heart is broad, the timber straightens of itself.
